title: Great but I’d like to have customization
body:
Great app. But I’d love to see options of customizing the widget.  
I’ve purchased a subscription a while ago. But I didn’t end up using it much, and then I tried to figure out why as I’m always curious why my brain wants or doesn’t want to do something.
I feel like the reason is that the widget is hard to see: low contrast text on blurry background. It’s mostly those circles of different colors but the text that is barely visible for me, it doesn’t “read into brain” right away. 
So my brain is not tricked to click “done” on those circles as it takes a while to figure what exact circle i need (my vision is fine, but I do have ADHD). 
So it feels like I loose more dopamine for finding the right circle than getting a dopamine for hitting a circle as an  award for completing the habit. 
Also, I realized that habits as a list with check marks ✅ works better to motivate my brain, so I moved to a different app for now. Also, high contrast is what helps (like simple black text on white background).  
But I hope new accessibility features will be added to this one as overall it’s functionality is great.
Thank you for your work ❤️

title: Premium features not worth premium price
body:
The base app is OK. It’s interesting that there’s a proprietary algorithm to determine how strong a habit is. 

On the other hand, I regret purchasing a premium subscription already. It seems unlocking unlimited habits is the only benefit. Fine, but what about adding something actually innovative like habit tracking within a given day? For example, if I’m trying to form the habit of drinking at least four liters of water a day, then the app could let me check off each time I drink a liter. The devs could just add a check or count for each sub-habit and feed that into whatever variable, etc the app counts as the overarching habit. 

This is just one simple idea. I’m sure there are many more features which could be added to make premium worth it. As it stands, I cannot recommend the premium subscription and would recommend trying other Habit apps before committing to this Habit lol

title: False Advertising
body:
I downloaded the app after reading these exact words on the product page:

”Why more than 900,000 users choose Daily Habit Tracker?

1. Unlimited amount of habits. You don’t need to pay a penny to start building as many habits as you need.
2. Ad-free. We hate ads & don’t want to bother our users”

Here’s how that went: 
- Opened the app
- Greeted with a prompt to pay for premium. 
- Dismissed the prompt. 
- Premium prompt pops up again.
(“Hmm.. that’s kind of annoying..”)
- Dismissed the prompt again.
- Started creating my first habit.
- Tried to change the color.
- Premium prompt pops up again.
- Dismissed a third time.
- Finished creating habit (minor complaint here; you can’t set the frequency to more than once a day, e.g. twice a day).
- Created two more habits.
- Tried to create a fourth.
- Premium prompt pops up again.
- Dismissed a fourth time.
(“Surely that’s a mistake..? I was promised unlimited habits, for not even a penny.”)
- Tried to create a fourth habit.
- Premium prompt pops up again.
- Dismissed a fifth and final time.
- Uninstalled.

To be fair, the interface is pretty nice and polished. Please correct me if I’m stupid and missing something obvious, but why can’t I create more than 3 habits? I thought this app could help me structure my day and hold me accountable with reaching my goals. I don’t need an app to remind me of a maximum of 3 things. 

The premium pop-ups are a minor annoyance, and I understand that the creators need to make money. I just found their incredible frequency ironic after they touted, “We hate ads & don’t want to bother our users.” They’re a bit bothersome to be honest.

title: It was good at first, but then they added the “New Year, New Me” offer...
body:

It made it super easy to keep track of my habits, goals, and things I wanted to do more often like drink water and go outside to take a walk. But then 2021 came around and they added an offer called “New Year, New Me.” Current users of the app may know what I’m talking about. Anyways, they have been sending me nonstop “claim your offer now” notifications ever since and every time I open the app it says “__ hours left to claim your offer!” But then once that timer is up, a new one begins right after. I usually would just ignore all this and it wouldn’t phase me much, but the fact that it won’t let me add any new habits unless I pay money for the “New Year, New Me” offer is the cherry on top. And before you ask, yes, I did try deleting one of my other habits, seeing if I was just at the limit of how many habits the app allows. But alas, it still would not let me start a new habit and now the other habits I’ve deleted are gone! So, in conclusion, I would have given this app a 5-star review if it weren’t for that “New Year, New Me” offer that they keep trying to shove down my throat. Like, I get that you want to advertise it, but... chill! If the app creator/developer is seeing this, I would love if you would just stop promoting the offer when a user of the app has clearly shown no interest in purchasing it. And who knows, maybe I would have considered purchasing it if you hadn’t spammed me with the offer every 2 seconds!

(PS, totally not trying to be bitter or mean here, I just want to warn others before downloading this app of what they’re getting themselves into. Also, I’m hoping to be able to add some more habits without having to pay money, or at least get my old ones back. :)

title: Amazing app, feel betrayed by dev.
body:
This app was my favourite. I used it to track my habits, and it worked magnificently - the best feature is being able to check off/uncheck the past few days, great if you forgot to check it off. I liked this app so much, I even spent money ‘donating’ to the dev, because it was free, and worth it (it also unlocked features like dark mode and customizable colours).

As to the subscription, having used this app for a while, I would be willing to pay $10-$15 per year, but even the promo price of $20 is too high in my opinion.

I don’t mind subscription models - they’re the only sustainable way for developers to keep working on an app. My problem here is that the dev TOOK AWAY features from what it was before. I paid for dark mode as a one-time purchase. I used the reminder delay feature. As a final note to other people, be wary before you pay anything; read below.

To the developer: this is absolutely atrocious behaviour. I paid for features, and you’ve taken them away. I realize you need to make money sustainably, and it’s your right to do this. I might have even paid for the subscription, had I not had this experience. But treating people who’ve paid you in the past this way is not at all acceptable. I would hope that you don’t realize this has happened, and are going to fix it, but in general this has not happened when other apps have moved to subscription models, so I can’t really even hope for it here. I cannot understate how exploitative this is; treating paying customers like this is completely unacceptable. You’re probably going to make a lot more money, and my voice will be drowned out, but I refuse point blank to pay again, or repetitively, for something I’ve already paid for. This is utterly despicable and of low behaviour, which shows a complete lack of ethical consideration for your actions.

Edit: this is a violation of App Store rules, and I have taken steps to report this to Apple. You are required to grandfather previously purchased functionality when transferring your app to a subscription model under App Store Review Guidelines section 3.1.2(a), or you risk having your app removed from the App Store. Fix this immediately.

title: The best for sticking with a habit
body: I’ve tried many habit trackers and they never work for me, as most focus too much on “streaks” or not breaking the chain. The best thing is that missing a day or two doesn’t ruin your score. However, miss several days or a week and you start to see your score go down so you are motivated to keep doing the habit to maintain your score or keep growing it. When starting a new habit, your score grows quickly which is very motivating! I have one habit that I was trying to do 3 times a week but I’m doing it almost every day thanks to this app! I also love how easy it is to see all your habits at once and quickly check them off for that day because today is on the far right. Other apps I’ve used are not this easy. I enjoy looking at the calendar for each habit occasionally, but mostly just stay on the main screen.

title: Great concept, needs new algorithm.
body:
So, between being a mom of two and having horrible anxiety, my memory is nonexistent. Adding depression in the mix I have a hard time getting things done. I have to admit, this app has helped a LOT. I have successfully used it daily for a month now and it helps me remember when I do certain things (as in showering) and making sure I feed and walk my dogs twice a day and don’t forget. I can honestly say this IS the best app for it.

BUT. I do not want to give it 5 stars because LOGICALLY, their formula doesn’t make ANY sense to me. The first day you complete a habit, it stays at zero. The next day, it goes to three. According to their page, it “takes 91 days to complete a habit”. But REALISTICALLY, if I start tracking how often I can continue a streak, the first time I do it, it’s 100%. If I do it again, the next day my streak would also be 100%. BUT, If I miss the 3rd day, I would no longer have 100%. SO, what I’m trying to say is that it would be SO much more motivating if it started at 100% because I would be much more likely to fight to keep my 100% than to see small numbers and have to take 3 whole months just to complete it.

title: First review of any app! TLDR: This App Rocks
body: This is my first time reviewing any app on the app store and I have used iPhones since the 4s. This really helped me nail the habit I’ve been wanting to pick up the most and thats journaling. Along side journaling, I also implemented drinking tea into my routine. I found that writing myself how long a habit takes to complete in the “Motivate Yourself” section helps a lot in motivating me to get that habit completed. I would suggest taking small habits and building off those. The design is really neat, showing off your percentages of how far along you are into your habit. Reaching a 100 percent is really nice, but I found that I actually have built the habit even before hitting 100 percent completion. Around the time I usually journal I can, almost everyday, remind myself before the app reminds me and I think that speaks volumes about the app. This app is a great tool to have, but like all tools you must know how to work with it. Luckily, this app is super intuitive and it’s easy to build steam with this app and get a few wins under your belt to feel accomplished as you see your percentage reach closer and closer to 100 percent. Definitely recommend this app, poke around with it before you dive in, get a feel then set your first habit you’d like to form, you won’t be disappointed! :)

title: Lots of potential
body:
This app is very aesthetically pleasing, and intuitive. Unfortunately, it’s missing several features that make it less then ideal.
1) Notifications. They don’t work. The app is set to remind me about my habits, but I’m forced to pick a time to be reminded. Because of this the notification badge will only appear after I’ve been reminded, but they ALL go away when I open the app, regardless of wether or not I’ve completed any habits. The notification badge should reflect the amount of incomplete tasks, so if I have 3 in incomplete habits, there should be a notification badge on the app with a 3. 
2) Habit tracking needs some work. If I start a new habit to do every day, and then complete it, you would think I would have a 100% for that habit. That’s not how it works, in fact I can’t figure out how it works, from what I can tell it adds 10% or so, so even when you’ve completed a habit 100% of the time, it takes awhile for that habit to actually say that.
3) Organization. The app is to simple. I should be able to organize different Categories of habits rather then have 1 long list of all my habits. I should also be able to organize habits based on how often I’ve set them to be accomplished. For example, if you have a habit set to be done every other day, it looks exactly like a habit set to be done every day. The app should make it clear that I don’t need to do a habit today because I did it yesterday. 
Overall, the app is a great start. By fixing these small problems the app would 100% be a 5 star app. However, these small problems add up, and create an app that just really isn’t all that useful. The point of this app is to help people keep there habits, but because you have to go out of your way to use the app, I end up rarely using it.

title: Minimalist design, ease of use, needs more features
body:
I’m no stranger to self-help and productivity apps. I have tried a great deal of them from Habitica to ToDoist. I was looking for a more streamlined, easy to view habit tracker that wouldn’t take much space, time, nor thought to operate. 

Habit- Daily Tracker is great for ease of use, and simplistic design. All of the features of the app are accessible from a quick swipe or tap, and the learning curve to use the app is minimal. I enjoy the simple colorful design, and the data charts offered are easy to read and comprehensive. 

I do enjoy the app, however it needs updated features. One such example is the ability to schedule a habit to be repeated more than once per day. For example “brush teeth,” if I want to complete this habit twice daily, I have to make two habits and track them separately. Likewise, you have a limit on how many habits you can track, again stifling options. 

I contributed $2.99 to the developer because of the beautiful design and ease of use. I am hopeful that additional features will be added in the future.
